name: Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Reported in multiple ethnicities including Middle Eastern, Indian, and European populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple subcutaneous nodules predominantly on the scalp, ears, and back
Severe gingival hypertrophy causing feeding difficulties
Progressive joint contractures and stiffness limiting mobility
Histopathological confirmation of hyaline material deposition in skin or connective tissue biopsy
Episodes of recurrent infections and protein-losing enteropathy
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the ANTXR2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features (cutaneous nodules, gingival hypertrophy, joint contractures) plus histopathological confirmation or biallelic pathogenic variants in ANTXR2 gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; early diagnosis is critical for management and genetic counseling.

searchTerms: multiple small firm lumps under skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive joint contractures with limited range of motion

common.symptomName: Recurrent infections due to immunological compromise
searchTerms: frequent infections due to weak immunity

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
searchTerms: poor growth due to feeding problems
failure to gain weight from eating difficulties
brown patches on elbows or knees
loose stools related to gut problems
watery bowel movements due to GI involvement

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to joint stiffness
searchTerms: delayed walking or movement due to stiff joints
slow motor development from joint tightness
late motor milestones because of joint stiffness

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to chronic disease
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to long-term disease

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to lung restriction
respiratory problems caused by limited lung expansion

imaging: X-rays showing joint contractures and osteopenia
MRI may show soft tissue nodules with hyaline deposits
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ANTXR2 (CMG2) gene
other: Histopathology demonstrating eosinophilic hyaline material deposition in dermis and connective tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of lipid-laden histiocytes rather than hyaline deposits
Lack of gingival hypertrophy and joint contractures
Presence of coarse facial features and organomegaly
Different genetic mutations and enzyme deficiencies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive joint contractures limiting mobility
Severe gingival hypertrophy causing feeding difficulties
references: Nofal A, et al. Hyaline fibromatosis syndrome: clinical and molecular insights. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020.
Hanks S, et al. Mutations in ANTXR2 cause juvenile hyaline fibromatosis and infantile systemic hyalinosis. Nat Genet. 2003.
Orphanet: Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome. Orphanet Report Series, 2024.
